note_claims.claim: The presenting complaint is fever and right earache.
Fever started since Tuesday evening (2 days), with a maximum temperature of 38.9 °C at home.
Patient pulls at the right ear and was unsettled overnight.
Patient eats less but drinks well, and passes urine normally.
Patient vomited once on Tuesday, but has not vomited since.
No diarrhoea.
Coryza (runny nose) for about a week preceded the current symptoms.
No rash.
Patient's brother had chickenpox two weeks ago, and the patient has not had chickenpox.
Patient is alert and playing this morning.
No breathing difficulty.
Patient was previously well and immunisations are up to date.
Paracetamol has been given intermittently.
Patient takes no regular medicines.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient weighs 14 kilograms.
Patient's temperature is 38.4 °C, heart rate is 130, and breathing rate is 26.
Patient's hands and feet are warm, and capillary refill is under two seconds.
The left eardrum is normal.
The right eardrum is red and bulging.
The patient's throat is mildly erythematous.
Impression is Right acute otitis media.
Contact GP or 111 if fever lasts more than 5 days in total, if there is ear discharge, or if the condition does not improve after three days.
Report if the patient develops chickenpox and seems very unwell.

transcript_facts.fact: The clinician greeted the patient by name (Poppy).
The patient has had a temperature and keeps pulling at her ear.
The duration of the fever was corrected from two days to three days, starting Monday evening (the night of her swimming lesson).
The temperature measured last night was 38.9 °C.
The patient has been pulling at the right ear, mostly.
The patient reports that her ear hurts.
The patient is not eating much but is drinking juice and milk.
The patient is in pants during the day but is still weeing normally, a few times today already.
The patient was sick once on Tuesday, but has not been sick since.
The patient has had a runny nose for about a week before the current symptoms started.
The patient has no rash.
The patient has never had chickenpox.
The patient is grumpy but herself and was playing with her brother this morning.
The patient reports no problems breathing.
The patient is healthy and all her vaccinations are up to date.
The patient takes no regular medicines and has no known drug allergies.
The patient has been given Calpol only when she seems really bad.
The patient weighs 14 kilograms.
The patient's temperature is 38.4 °C, heart rate is 130, and breathing rate is 26.
The patient's hands and feet are warm and the capillary refill is under two seconds.
The left eardrum looks normal.
The right eardrum is red and bulging.
The patient's throat is a little red.
There is no rash on the patient's skin.
The clinician suggests the condition looks like a middle ear infection on the right side.
The clinician suggests giving the patient paracetamol 180 milligrams (7.5 mL of 120 mg/5 mL infant suspension) up to four times a day for pain.
The clinician suggests giving the patient ibuprofen 100 milligrams (5 mL of 100 mg/5 mL suspension) three times a day with food for pain.
The clinician will provide a back-up prescription for amoxicillin 250 milligrams three times a day for 5 days.

Urgent signs requiring immediate attention include developing a rash that doesn't fade when pressed with a glass, becoming very drowsy or hard to wake, struggling to breathe, or stopping drinking and not weeing.
The patient should contact the clinic or 111 if the fever lasts more than five days in total, if there is any discharge from her ear, or if she is not improving after three days.
The clinician advises that the patient may get chickenpox in the next week or so since she has been exposed.
